correctness.rationale: The orthogonal projectors E, B-E and W_i form a complete spectral decomposition with eigenvalues 0,n,n-a_i. All three entry forms are explicitly calculated. Positivity conditions suffice termwise; necessity follows by K2 edge signs, arbitrary cliques at rescaled steps, and within-part K_{p,q} signs followed by rational-density continuity. The Padé numerator is (s-3)^2+3, its denominator exceeds it by 12s, and its divided quotient has strictly negative derivative. All quantifiers and boundary cases are explicit. Independently constructed direct rational matrices exactly match the projector expression and strictly positive row-stochastic entries on 993 graph-step cases; finite checks are auxiliary, not a replacement for the universal proof. No unstated spectral or matrix inverse assumptions are needed because all denominators are positive on s>=0.

value.rationale: This is a sharp reusable characterization of a natural family of diffusion operators, not merely a check on one tiny graph. Complete multipartite graphs include stars, cliques and arbitrary bicliques with unbounded degree heterogeneity and order. The offdiagonal same-part type forces a nontrivial independent divided-difference shape restriction, and the f(s)=1/(1+s^2) counterexample shows scalar positivity is not enough. The criterion gives a principled design/test for infinitely many rational or continuous spectral steppers. It explains mathematically how a fourth-order Gauss stability map whose unrestricted absolute-monotonicity radius is zero nevertheless yields positive, conservative diffusion for all steps on this large structured graph class, with limits stated explicitly; this is a meaningful structural boundary rather than a routine parameter perturbation.
